{'index': 0, 'translation': 'The screen sizes of the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max are expected to remain the same as their predecessors, but reports suggest their displays will see upgrades in two other areas. Here are the key highlights.'}

{'index': 1, 'translation': '#1: LTPO+ Technology'}

{'index': 2, 'translation': 'LTPO has long been the technology powering the iPhone\'s "Always-On Display" and ProMotion features. With the iPhone 18 Pro, Apple is reportedly upgrading to the more advanced LTPO+.'}

{'index': 3, 'translation': 'The benefits of LTPO+ include reduced screen flickering through more sensitive adjustments in low-light environments and improved power efficiency. In other words, iPhone 18 Pro users can enjoy more stable display performance while consuming less power.'}

{'index': 4, 'translation': '#2: Smaller Dynamic Island Cutout'}

{'index': 5, 'translation': 'The displays on the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max are also expected to feature a smaller Dynamic Island cutout, slightly increasing the actual usable screen area.'}

{'index': 6, 'translation': 'The new Dynamic Island is reportedly about 35% smaller than that of the iPhone 17 Pro. This size has even been hinted at in the new Siri design within iOS 27.'}

{'index': 7, 'translation': 'Apple first introduced the Dynamic Island on the iPhone 14 Pro in 2022. While software features related to the Dynamic Island and "Live Activities" have expanded significantly over the years, the physical cutout itself has remained unchanged.'}

{'index': 8, 'translation': 'With the launch of the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, Apple is finally taking a step closer to the dream of a truly "zero-cutout" display.'}

{'index': 9, 'translation': "What other changes would you like to see in the iPhone's display? Let us know in the comments below."}
